w: The local counselor met Swamishri and said, "This mandir has increased the beauty of this borough. Whenever I come here I feel that I have come nearer to God and heaven. I experience peace in coming here."
Due to Swamishri's back pain, slight pain in the heart and stomach, he was advised by doctors to rest as much as possible.
In the evening, Swamishri arrived for the Sharad Punam festival at 9.20 pm. More than 23,000 devotees had assembled for the festival.

The discourses centred upon the glory of Gunatitanand Swami. The four dramas enacted depicted the power of Swaminarayan Mahamantra, the staunch faith of Abhaysinh Darbar who did not succumb to mantra-jantra to relieve his fever, Gunatitanand Swami who tolerated the persecution of Uga Khuman and blessed him in return and Yogiji Maharaj who was bitten by a black cobra in Gondal and saved by the chanting of the mahamantra. A lively folk dance appropriate for the occasion added enthusiasm and joy to the festival. Finally, Swamishri blessed the congregation by referring to Gunatitanand Swami's boldness in speaking about the supreme glory of Shriji Maharaj.
Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was honored by devotees.

Guest Opinion: Dr Faizal Zeerah, President and CEO of International Hospital, Bahrain, opined, “I had seen the place a year ago and I have seen it today and there are no words that I can use to describe it. I have seen love expressed in its most glorious picture and I have seen devotion to a cause, to a principle which is overwhelming. “Pramukh Swami is somebody that all of us love and adore. He has changed people’s lives, including my own and many others by touching their lives with his love, affection and his dedication to make this place a better world. And this monument – that he is the force behind – talks a lot about Pramukh Swami more than anybody can describe.”
Durgeshbhai, son of Bhupatsinh, had come from Jasdan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Bhupat was this big, and now you have retired. What do you do now?"
Durgeshbhai said, "Just that, I have retired."
Swamishri said, "It's fine that you have retired, but bhajan is being done, isn't it? Now that we have retired, we should bring everyone into satsang, do bhajan and devotion and help others do it."
Durgeshbhai, the son of Bhupatsinh, had come from Jasdan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Bhupat was this small, and now you have retired. What do you do now?"
Durgeshbhai said, "Nothing much, I have retired."

Swamishri said, "It does not matter that you have retired, but bhajan is still being done, isn't it? Now that we have retired, we should help everyone do satsang, and do bhajan and devotion ourselves and help others do it too."
